subject: General Knowledge
description: Regional and religious festivals of India

questions.stem: 'Onam' — the harvest festival associated with the legendary king Mahabali — is celebrated mainly in:
questions.explanation: Onam — 10-day harvest festival of Kerala, during the Malayalam month of Chingam (August-September). Celebrates the legendary return of King Mahabali. Features — pookalam (floral carpet), Onasadya (feast on banana leaf), Vallamkali (snake-boat race) on the Pamba river, and traditional dances like Thiruvathira. It is secular — celebrated by people of all faiths.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the festival with the state it is closely associated with. A. Bihu. B. Pongal. C. Lohri. D. Chhath. List-II: 1. Assam, 2. Tamil Nadu, 3. Punjab, 4. Bihar.
questions.explanation: Bihu — Assam's new-year/harvest festival. Pongal — Tamil Nadu's four-day harvest festival in January. Lohri — Punjab winter bonfire festival in mid-January, with sarson da saag and makki di roti. Chhath — Bihar (and eastern UP / Jharkhand) — 4-day Sun worship, praying to Chhathi Maiya.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'Hornbill Festival' — a 10-day cultural showcase of tribal traditions — is held every December in:
questions.explanation: Hornbill Festival — held at Kisama Heritage Village, near Kohima, 1-10 December — showcases the culture of Nagaland's Naga tribes. It began in 2000 to promote cultural tourism. Named after the Great Indian Hornbill, a bird revered in Naga folklore. Other NE festivals worth knowing — Wangala (Garo, Meghalaya), Chapchar Kut (Mizoram), Sangken (Arunachal).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Rann Utsav' — a 3-month cultural festival over the white salt marsh — is held in:
questions.explanation: Rann Utsav — Gujarat Tourism's annual festival (typically November-February) held at Dhordo in the Great Rann of Kachchh. Tent city, folk performances, camel safaris, moonlight nights over the white salt desert. Neighbouring Rajasthan has the Pushkar Camel Fair and the Jaisalmer Desert Festival. Kachchh was designated the 'Best Tourism Village' by UNWTO (Dhordo) in 2023.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Rath Yatra festival — with massive wooden chariots of the deities Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra — takes place at:
questions.explanation: Puri's Rath Yatra (usually in Ashadha, June-July) is one of India's most ancient pilgrimages — the three deities are pulled in enormous chariots from the 12th-century Jagannath temple to the Gundicha temple, 3 km away. Lakhs of devotees pull the chariots. The English word 'juggernaut' comes from 'Jagannath'. Konark is famous for the Sun Temple (UNESCO WHS); Cuttack for Bali Yatra; Bhubaneswar is the capital of Odisha.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'Losar' — the New Year festival — is mainly celebrated by the Buddhist communities of:
questions.explanation: Losar — Tibetan Buddhist new-year festival — observed in Ladakh, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal (Spiti) and by Tibetan communities elsewhere. Typically in February, lasts about 15 days. Marked by monastic dances (cham), prayer-flag raising, family gatherings. The Hemis festival (Ladakh, June-July) and Saga Dawa (celebrating Buddha's birth / enlightenment / nirvana, May-June) are other major Himalayan Buddhist festivals.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'Baisakhi' — the traditional harvest festival of Punjab — also commemorates the founding of which religious order?
questions.explanation: Baisakhi — 13/14 April, the start of the Punjabi solar new year. Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa Panth at Anandpur Sahib on Baisakhi of 1699 — initiating the Panj Pyare (Five Beloved) and giving the Sikhs their five Ks (kesh, kanga, kara, kachera, kirpan). Ranjit Singh was crowned Maharaja of Punjab on Baisakhi, 1801. Tragically, the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919) also fell on Baisakhi.
